holidays.name: National Dessert Day
holidays.description: The day is an official excuse to skip the 'should I?' debate and go straight to the sweet course. Cake, pie, ice cream and anything else sugary all qualify.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance with no clearly documented founder. It has become a yearly favorite on the food-holiday calendar.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dessert' comes from the French 'desservir', which means 'to clear the table'. Originally, dessert was what you ate after the table was cleared.

holidays.name: Be Bald and Be Free Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates baldness and the confidence of people who wear it proudly. That includes people who are bald by choice, by genetics, or because of medical conditions like alopecia or cancer treatment. Sunscreen on the scalp is encouraged.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages self-acceptance and freedom from worrying about hair.
holidays.funFact: Many Roman emperors were famously sensitive about thinning hair. Julius Caesar reportedly combed his hair forward and liked to wear a laurel wreath.

holidays.name: National Pet Obesity Awareness Day
holidays.description: This day is a reminder to check whether Fluffy and Fido are carrying a few extra treats' worth of weight. It encourages more walks, more play and smaller portions to help pets avoid problems like heart disease and joint pain.
holidays.origin: It was started by the Association for Pet Obesity Prevention, which holds the observance each year to raise awareness of weight-related health risks in pets.
holidays.funFact: The Association for Pet Obesity Prevention surveys vets every year. The surveys have found that a majority of dogs and cats in the U.S. are overweight or obese.
